content: A bedtime story is a traditional practice in which a story is narrated to a child at bedtime to help them transition into sleep. This practice offers numerous benefits for both the adult storyteller, often a parent, and the child. Establishing a consistent routine of telling a bedtime story has a calming effect on the child, as the soothing tone of the storyteller’s voice helps the child relax and fall asleep more easily. The emotional connection fostered during this time strengthens the bond between the storyteller and the listener, creating a sense of closeness and security. Bedtime stories can either be read from a book or improvised as fictional tales created by the storyteller. These stories are typically brief, lasting between one and five minutes, and often conclude with a happy ending to leave the child with a sense of comfort and positivity. An alternative approach to bedtime storytelling involves reading longer narratives but dividing them into segments, ending each session with a cliffhanger. This method builds anticipation and excitement, as children eagerly look forward to the continuation of the story the following night. Over time, this practice establishes a structured and enjoyable bedtime routine.
